objective_for_doctor: A 54-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: shortness of breath.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m having significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing. I also have red skin lesions/redness on my cheek (left) and nose, and I have painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how long have you had the shortness of breath, and is it worse with exertion or when lying flat?  
Doctor: Do you have fever, chest pain, cough, or wheezing?  
Doctor: For the face rash and painful mouth ulcers: when did they start, and do they look like small sores inside the mouth or larger ulcers with bleeding?
I don’t know. My symptoms include painful mouth ulcers or sores, and red skin lesions/redness on my cheek (left) and nose.

Doctor: I’m going to examine you—right now, can you check your breathing: are you having any wheezing/stridor, and do you notice swelling of your lips/tongue or a skin rash elsewhere (besides the left cheek and nose)?  
Doctor: Also, have you had any new medications, recent infections, or do you smoke—while your mouth sores and breathing trouble have been going on (even approximately)?
I smoke cigarettes. I don’t know about any new medications or recent infections. I don’t know about wheezing/stridor or swelling of my lips/tongue.

Doctor: On exam, do you have oxygen saturation readings, and I’m going to order tests—REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry, REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Diff.  
Doctor: Also, do the mouth ulcers make it painful to swallow, and have you noticed any similar skin lesions on your eyes (red or painful eyes) or on other body areas?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I need a few key details—are your mouth ulcers painful to swallow, and have you had any eye redness/pain or vision changes?  
Doctor: Also, when did the rash and mouth ulcers start relative to the shortness of breath (same day, before, or after)?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Dermatology_Skin_Exam_and_Possible_Skin_Biopsy (perioral/cheek/nose lesions); REQUEST TEST: HIV_Test and REQUEST TEST: ESR_CRP.
I don’t know.

Doctor: I’m going to ask directly—can you describe the face rash: is it a butterfly-shaped rash with sparing of the nasolabial folds, or more like acne/follicular bumps or a scaly plaque? Also, are the mouth ulcers recurrent and do you get joint pains or new swelling anywhere?  
Doctor: Given your smoking plus shortness of breath, I also want to know: did the breathing start suddenly over hours–days, or gradually over weeks?
I don't know. I smoke cigarettes. I also have red skin lesions/redness on my left cheek and nose, and painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m going to check for urgency—right now, are you able to speak full sentences, and do you have any chest pain, hemoptysis (coughing blood), or severe sudden worsening of breathing?  
Doctor: Also, have you lost weight, had persistent fevers/night sweats, or noticed swollen lymph nodes (neck/armpits)?
I don’t know. I smoke cigarettes. I also have significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, red skin lesions/redness on my left cheek and nose, and painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m concerned this combination—shortness of breath plus a malar/periorificial facial rash and painful mouth ulcers—could represent an autoimmune mucocutaneous disease or an infection like HIV–related disease, so I’d like urgent objective data: REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry and REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas.  
Doctor: Next, I need to clarify whether the rash distribution is classic “malar” (over cheeks/bridge with possible nose involvement) and whether the mouth ulcers are painless or very painful—are they tender and do you see them on the tongue, gums, or palate?
I don’t know.

Doctor: I can’t decide without a few more specifics—are the mouth ulcers **painless or very painful**, and are they **small round/white (“aphthous”)** versus **large/deep**? Also, does your facial redness **spare the nasolabial folds** (the lines from nose to mouth), and is it **worse after sunlight**?
I don’t know. I smoke cigarettes. I also have significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, red skin lesions/redness on my left cheek and nose, and painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m going to ask just two quick, high-yield questions—are the mouth ulcers *painless small white/yellow sores* (like aphthae) or *large deep ulcers*, and is the facial rash *photosensitive* (worse after sun)?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any history of autoimmune disease or can you think of any new medication in the past 1–3 months (including antibiotics or seizure meds)?
I don’t know. I smoke cigarettes. I also have significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, red skin lesions/redness on my left cheek and nose, and painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m still missing the key differentiators, so I’ll focus on safety—are you in distress right now (can you speak full sentences), and do you have fever or chest pain?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Urgent_CBC_with_Diff_and_BMP; REQUEST TEST: HIV_p24_Antigen_plus_HIV_Ab; REQUEST TEST: ANA_with_Reflex_to_dsDNA_Smith; REQUEST TEST: Serum_Complement_C3_C4; REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA_or_CTPA_if_hypoxic_or_dyspneic_unexplained.
I don’t know. I smoke cigarettes. I’m having significant shortness of breath or difficulty breathing, red skin lesions/redness on my left cheek and nose, and painful mouth ulcers or sores.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this is potentially serious: your facial redness (cheek/nose) plus painful mouth ulcers with significant shortness of breath raises concern for autoimmune mucocutaneous disease (e.g., lupus) or HIV-related disease. I’m going to proceed assuming immediate evaluation—REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry, REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA_or_CTPA_if_hypoxic_or_dyspneic_unexplained.  
Doctor: While those results come, do you have any chest pain, coughing blood, or are you unable to speak full sentences due to breathlessness?  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with mucocutaneous involvement (malar/periorificial dermatitis and oral ulcers) causing/associated with dyspnea—must urgently rule out pulmonary embolism, infection (including HIV), and severe cardiopulmonary involvement.
